newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH NPF SEES HOPE FOR STEELMILL AFTER BANKRUPTCY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH NPF SEES HOPE FOR STEELMILL AFTER BANKRUPTCY.

text.p: The Czech National Fund (NPF), the government's privatisation agency, said on Friday it hoped fast bankruptcy proceedings would lead to an early restoration of production at the privately held Poldi Ocel steelworks.
"The NPF is welcoming.. the court declared bankruptcy over Poldi, because hesitation only made the situation more difficult, and increased losses," the fund said in a statement.

It quoted NPF chairman Roman Ceska as saying that he was convinced the bankruptcy procedings would be completed without "length complications so that production...could be renewed as quickly as possible".
Earlier this week a Prague commercial court declared Poldi Ocel s.r.o., based in the city of Kladno northwest of Prague, bankrupt, appointing an administrator to direct the sales of its assets.
The NPF is a minority shareholder in the company which has debts reportedly reaching eight billion crowns.

A 54.8 percent stake is owned by the privately-held Bohemia Art, which acquired Poldi under a government privatisation plan, but failed to pay the NPF fully for its stake while the firm fell into insolvency production ceased.
The government has made clear it intended to save production at Poldi, which produces, among other items, high-grade steels for precision machine toods.

It is not yet clear if Poldi will be fully liquidiated, sold in pieces, or as a whole in order to satisfy the demands of creditors who range from the state social security authority to the NPF to several banks and employees who have not been paid in months.

Bohemia Art changed hands just a day before the bankruptcy was declared. Its original owners, Vladimir Stehlik and Marko Stehlik, are facing a criminal investigation and have been charged with abuse of commercial information.
The new owner, a little-known Czech firm called ProWin lost its ownership rights after the appoionted the administrator.
Poldi used to employ some 6,000 workers, but many have left due to unpaid wages and poor future prospects. Production has been virtually shut for several months.
